sections.html: Synodontis voltae Roman, 1975. Type locality: Bougouriba River, Upper Volta. Size: 147 mm SL (14.7 cm). IUCN Red List: Data Deficient (last assessed 2019).

Lay the fish in your hand with its head toward your palm and the tail toward your fingers. Hold the dorsal spine between your middle and ring finger so the fish is belly up, so you won't be punctured by the sharp fin spines. The genital pore is in a small furrow of tissue (in healthy fish) and is obstructed by the pelvic fins. Pull down on the tail gently to arch the spine; the pelvic fins will stand and the furrow open to display the genital pore and the anus. The male has a somewhat ridged genital papilla on which the spermatoduct is on the back side, facing the tail fin. A gravid female also shows an extended papilla but the oviduct is on the ventral side of the papilla. It may also show a little redness if gravid. A thin or emaciated female will have just two pink pores, the oviduct and the anus.

All species in the genus Synodontis have a hardened head cap with a humeral process behind the gill opening, pointed toward the posterior. The dorsal and pectoral fins have a hardened, serrated first ray. The caudal fin is always forked. There is one pair of maxillary barbels, sometimes with membranes and occasionally branched. The two pairs of mandibular barbels are often branched and can have nodes. The cone-shaped teeth in the upper jaw are short; those in the lower jaw are S-shaped and movable. These fish produce audible sounds when disturbed by rubbing the base of the pectoral spine against the pectoral girdle.

No breeding report exists.
